You are fixing a bug in the Python repository in the current working directory. The bug and the required behavior are described below. Read the relevant source files, make the necessary code edits to the source (do NOT edit the tests), and use the shell to run the tests to confirm your fix. Keep changes minimal.

ISSUE:
Removing a default header of a session
[The docs](http://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/user/advanced/#session-objects) say that you can prevent sending a session header by setting the headers value to None in the method's arguments. You would expect (as [discussed on IRC](https://botbot.me/freenode/python-requests/msg/10788170/)) that this would work for session's default headers, too:

``` python
session = requests.Session()
# Do not send Accept-Encoding
session.headers['Accept-Encoding'] = None
```

What happens is that "None"  gets sent as the value of header.

```
Accept-Encoding: None
```

For the reference, here is a way that works:

``` python
del session.headers['Accept-Encoding']
```



The test suite lives in tests/. You can run it with: python -m pytest -q
When the tests pass, you are done.
We need to find where session.headers is implemented. Search sessions.py.

We need to allow setting header None to remove. In Session.prepare_request merge_setting handles merging request.headers with self.headers. merge_setting removes keys set to None from merged dict (lines 57-60). But when session.headers['Accept-Encoding']=None, that sets in session headers dict a key mapping to None. Then merge_setting will treat request.headers as None? Wait: In prepare_request, request.headers is passed from Request(headers=...). In Session.request, they pass headers=headers param from method call; if user passes None default, then request.headers=None. But when setting session.headers['Accept-Encoding']=None, that modifies self.headers dict to have value None. merge_setting(request.headers, self.headers) will treat request_setting as None? Actually request_setting is request.headers which may be None. In merge_setting: if session_setting is None return request_setting; if request_setting is None return session_setting. So if request_setting=None and session_setting has key with None, it returns session_setting dict unchanged (including None). Then later in merge_setting for headers, after merging, they remove keys set to None from request_setting items. But request_setting was None so loop not executed. Thus header remains None.

Solution: modify Session.headers default to allow deletion? We can change default_headers to use CaseInsensitiveDict with values but if user sets None we want removal. Easiest: override __setitem__ in CaseInsensitiveDict? But simpler: modify merge_setting to treat session_setting entries with value None as delete even when request_setting is None. In merge_setting, after merging, they iterate over request_setting items and delete keys where v is None. Should also consider session_setting values None when request_setting is None. We can modify merge_setting accordingly.

Implement change in sessions.py at lines 57-60: add loop to remove keys from merged_setting if value None in either setting dicts? Actually we want that if session_setting has key with None, it should be removed from merged_setting regardless of request_setting. So after merging, iterate over both dicts and delete where v is None.

Implement patch.
We need to edit lines 57-60. Use Edit with old_string and new_string. Provide exact snippet.
